And Romano's remains a must destination to enjoy eating one. And here's a tip for you - they can ship them to anywhere in the USA and Canada. Cozy and sophisticated, the Riverbench tasting room near downtown SB is the perfect place to kick back and relax. The tasting room offers three flights: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, and Sparkling Wines. My boyfriend and I opted for the Chardonnay and Pinot Noir flights, both great options depending on your palette!

Here were some of our favorites:

2012 Riverbench Clone 115 Pinot Noir: A touch of hyacinth and dried black currant make this the standout in a sea of Pinot Noirs. Szechuan pepper gives you a perfect kick at the end!

2012 Riverbench Chapel View Chardonnay: light and versatile, a perfect chard for a night in with the girls or solo with a movie and some buttery popcorn. Needless to say, we bought two bottles!

As a San Franciscan, I'm spoiled by my close proximity to Napa and Sonoma. But Santa Barbara wine seems to be the new underdog in this state! Now if only they figure out an easier way to waive the tasting fees. Three bottles for one waived fee?  Ay caramba!

text:
I KNEW IT WOULD CLOSE!


Here's my review from just over 2 years ago, and it remained as valid as ever to the very last day they were open:

"This is the perfect example of what I imagine a middle-aged mainline business man or some other local variety of briefcase monkey thinks of as "hip".  Very nice looking interior screams of overwrought dollar signs: sleek looking but soulless and obviously the product of restauranteurs with FAR too much money to throw around.  But none the less, nice, new, clean, innocuous-looking place.  A few TV's playing local sports teams behind the relatively small and forgettable bar.  

Never have I seen so many service personnel standing around-nice to have a server to customer ratio of 1 to 2 I guess, but again, inefficiency and money-hemorrhaging abound.  Beer selection is sub-par, mostly macro and a few typical craft offerings.  I suppose cocktails are the reason people go here?  And I can't objectively comment on this as I did not partake.  

Food was a crippling disappointment- not just for the selection (which was as trite and antiquated as can be, by the way-the negative tone has nothing to do with volume of selection, as I also believe elephantine novel-sized menus are about as appealing as anal-exploratory surgery ) or the menu design, or the plateware, but the quality was utterly insulting and pathetic.  I ordered the Vegetable Platter (I believe that's what it was called) for I think $10.  What arrived was a row of hackneyed selections, 3 of which I can GUARANTEE came straight out of a #10 can from either Sysco or US Foods: roasted red peppers julienned straight from the can (I could taste the tin flavor still-not even doctored up with a basic marinade), pickled cauliflower, and some kind of (likely) Tuscan-style white bean preparation.  The other components were broccoli rape which had absolutely no seasoning, and grilled scallions/baby leeks, which again had no discernible seasoning or adornment.  All this was served with what I can only gasp in horror to say was a single slice of diner-style toasted white bread.  The whole thing tasted of refrigerator-burnt margarine or incredibly cheap butter which is stored unwrapped in a refrigerator.  Absolutely insulting to someone who has been a professional chef for over a decade; unforgivably bland and boring.  

Prices were definitely high for the above described food.  Beer was priced on par with local places, cocktails/booze I can't say.

Laughter is the only response I can justifiably give when asked about this place. "


Glad to see the free market creating a leveling force among financially bloated restauranteurs!

Our server, Matt, was friendly and attentive to our all of our questions and to our son who shared his name. It was nice of him to let us know rather than just charge us more and he was apologetic.

The house balsamic dressing was also good, quite sweet.

We passed on dessert and wound up with a $35 bill before the tip, which was on par with what we would have spent in a diner.  It won't be hard to find an excuse to go there again down the road.

Service can be spotty. I've had some really great experiences and pleasant servers, but I've also had a few sour servers that failed to deliver or were inattentive. Little details that are fulfilled happily elsewhere (ex. change for a meter that could then be added to the bill later) are typically not provided.

Food is limited here (my understanding is that C&B doesn't have a full kitchen), but what I've ordered I enjoy. Their hummus/pita plate is good, and the soup of the day usually delicious. Their take on macaroni and cheese, and their sandwiches fell flat. Usually, I plan on having drinks at The Cask & Barrel, and go elsewhere for food. 

 The Cask & Barrel does have a great drink selection with plenty of daily specials and promotions, so be sure to check this cozy and fun spot out during happy hour!

We picked up Sun Sushi tonight to have an end of the week treat. Currently, it's take out only and you can order online conveniently. Ordering was easy, and they texted when the order was ready, which was actually on the lower end of the 35-45 minute estimate. When I walked inside, my food was ready and I paid and left. One thing to keep in mind is their ordering process is awkward and is setup in a way that can trick people into double tipping. When you place your order, it asks for a tip (typical) but the default payment method is to pay in person. When you get there and they run your card, 20% of the receipt is a section for gratuity. So if you are not sure that you previously added a tip line from home, or your spouse picks up the order, there's a good chance Sun is getting a percentage tip on top of your total + tip from earlier. Not a big deal but something to keep in mind.

Peach French Toast was ordered at both brunches and is a star, thick fluffy pieces of bread cooked perfectly with actual pieces of peach and a light peachy syrup. The open face egg and cheese and sausage sandwich was very good, the croissant it was served on was lightly toasted and very light and flaky. But for regular coffee, it is quite good, and the waiter the first brunch was very good about keeping the cups full.

Overall a good choice if you're in the 21st and Sansom area, but I wouldn't really travel far to come here unless you're a homemade biscuit or Peach French toast aficionado.  Cost is as expected in a local brunch type place, $15-20 per person although our second brunch was a little cheaper because of the poor service I didn't feel compelled to leave much of a tip.

text:
My wife and I decided to try Prime 47 after hitting up most of the high-end steak spots in Indy over the last three months (St. Elmo's, Ruth's Chris downtown, Ruth's Chris at Ironworks, Tonys, and Capital Grille). The restaurant is beautiful. The space reminds me of an old school bank, one in which the manager had a large office on the second floor from where he could look down over the operations on the first. Our server was very pleasant and dressed in the typical old fashioned steakhouse short-white-coat style.

We started off with the fried shrimp and calamari. This was absolutely delicious. Because I'm not a fan of mayonnaise, we had them bring the sauces out on the side. There were two sources: a citrus aioli and a kung pao. The kung pao was ridiculously good. I had also ordered a salad, but this never came. That was actually OK because I didn't want to get too full prior to my steak.

I ordered the bone-in dry-aged ribeye priced at $87. My wife ordered the 8 ounce prime fillet. This is where the wheels came off. My steak looked beautiful when it came out and was cooked to a perfect medium-rare. Unfortunately though, the only thing I could taste when I bit into the first piece of rib cap was smoke and char. This flavor was so overwhelming that I couldn't even tell if the steak had been salted. It was the kind of flavor I would've been impressed with had it been a Kroger choice grade steak and cooked on a neighbor's outdoor grill during a pool party. For an $87 bone-in prime cut however, it was unacceptable. 

Fortunately our server could see that I was pretty upset with my steak; so he offered for me to try something else. So I ordered the Delmonico ribeye. This was actually brought out by the manager with his apologies from the kitchen. He asked me to cut into it to make sure it was cooked my liking. I felt incredibly embarrassed for him when I cut into it and it was cooked to a blue rare. You could tell he was very taken aback, saying something to the effect of: "oh they must have tried to rush it out of the kitchen." He took it back with no questions asked and stated that he would just take my steak off the bill entirely. A few  minutes later the manager brought the steak back to the table. This time it was perfectly cooked to medium-rare. Unfortunately though, it had the same flavor as the dry-aged I initially tried: overwhelmingly smoky/charred that completely drowned out the flavor of the beef. Since both the manager and our server had gone to such great lengths to try to make me happy, I did finish the steak to show my gratitude. I could just as easily have eaten a few bites and taking the rest home to re-purpose though. 

In terms of my wife's fillet, it was just OK. The taste of smoke and char was definitely not as dramatic, but the steak had very little flavor. It was also slightly undercooked: my wife ordered it medium, but it was definitely a solid medium-rare in the center. This actually worked out for me though, because I was able to try the portion of the steak that was too undercooked for her.

The only side we ordered was the truffle fries. These were delicious. Cooked to a beautiful crisp and perfectly seasoned. Our server did bring us out some broccoli, which Prime 47 is trying out is a new side offering. It was OK: probably a little too salty and just in general not a high-quality side you would expect to be served at a high-end prime steakhouse. Bringing this to our table though was another very nice gesture to make up for my disappointment with my steak. 

The final conciliatory gesture was being served a dessert cookie with ice cream and chocolate sauce, and 2 complementary glasses of the Prosecco we had been drinking. The cookie was outrageously delicious. Unfortunately, I could barely eat it by this point because I was so full. 

All in all, I would say that prime 47 is a beautiful restaurant with a very professional and dedicated staff that serves excellent sides and desserts, but seriously underwhelming steaks. I've definitely come to realize over the past few months that I prefer a broiled to a grilled steak. So I initially thought that a rating of three out of five stars might be a little harsh. However, the grilled tomahawk ribeye I recently had at St. Elmo's is still one of the best steaks I've ever eaten. So I can't completely attribute my dissatisfaction with the steaks I tried at Prime 47 to their having been grilled alone. I could also see how someone might  enjoy the almost rustic flavor of the steaks here. I just didn't. 

3/5
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The review is mixed, but overall negative due to the underwhelming steaks. The models are in moderate agreement, with BERT being the most confident in the 3-star rating.

text:
I really wanted to like NOLA. In fact, I really did like NOLA right up until the end of the night when my table was unceremoniously kicked out because we'd reached the 3 hour seating limit.

The food at NOLA was really good. The country fried chicken was amazing. The various seafood appetizers that we had were great, and their drink selection is pretty good. But there were problems. They were out of a lot of menu items which, considering we arrived at 6:30pm, seemed a bit strange. They were out of at least 4 items very early in the night and ran out of more items as the night went on.

On the night we were there they had no wings, no nachos, no sweet potato fries, no etouffee, and they ran out of coconut shrimp part-way through the evening. Things weren't off to a promising start, but we ordered from the items that they hadn't run out of them and thoroughly enjoyed them.

Because NOLA is also a live music venue, we had planned to stay around after our meal and continue to order drinks. This was fine until our server came up and told us that she had been informed that we had to leave in 15 minutes because another party had reserved our table. She had delivered new drinks to us just moments earlier, so this was unwelcome news. The first band hadn't even finished!

After some discussions with a very unhelpful manager -- apparently the waitress had to fight with him to get him to even apologize -- we learned that they have a policy of limiting parties to 3 hours at a table. If they weren't a live music venue, this would be understandable. But because they are a music venue, it seems odd to have a time limit that would make more sense at a traditional restaurant. Still, we wouldn't have minded if they'd informed us of this at the start of the evening (or, better yet, when we made our reservation).

The manager did tell us that he would try to find space for us toward the back of the room, but he never returned to our table. After we cleared up our bill and left -- now in a very bad mood -- we noticed that there were many empty tables. Surely, both our party and the party with the 9:15 reservation could have been accommodated.

It's a shame, because up until the moment that we were so rudely ejected from the restaurant, we were all really enjoying the scene and thinking that we would likely be regular customers. Instead of gaining 5 new regulars, NOLA lost 5 customers and gained a negative Yelp review.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The models agree on a 2-star rating with high confidence, indicating a strong consensus on the negative experience due to the time limit policy and poor service. The reviewer enjoyed the food but was turned off by the management's inflexibility and lack of communication.

Our friendly server told us there was a Happy Hour deal that ended at six o'clock.  Two cocktails or glasses of wine for the price of one, she said.  Any wine or cocktail priced $15 or less qualified and both beverages had to be the same kind, she said.  

Sounded like a pretty good deal to us.

The server handed us an IPad to review  specialty cocktail menu and wine lists.  She said she would come back to take our order as the IPad was not for ordering just for reading the menu.  Seemed redundant to us since cocktail menus and wine list were on the table.   

This is indicative of the "flash without function" that seems hallmark for the space.  "Oooh, Myrtle, look at this!  An Ipad." 

More goofiness masquerading as coolness that makes this place laughable. 

We settled on top shelf Margaritas.  The drinks arrived in a tall glass with lots of ice and mixer and a straw.  Not the worst we've ever had.  Not the best.  Still, at $10 each on the menu and in the "two for one" Happy Hour mode, we were feeling good about the bargain price of $5 a drink.  

But to our unhappy surprise, after nearly an hour had passed and we were nearing the bottom of our libations and getting ready to depart  our server arrived with two more drinks.  

Speechless for a moment (not often a state for me) I asked "Umm?  We didn't order these".  

Our nice server said THIS was the "two for one" at Happy Hour.  You order one and you get a second one free after you drink the first one. 

Our first response was to laugh at being "had".  But being long past wanting to or being able to have two cocktails and navigate, this was lost on me as "value".  It seems a pretty sophomoric policy of the bar to over serve two drinks to folks who only want one.  Just sayin'.  

Our server said we weren't the first customers to feel "had" by the policy.  Seems to me ownership is shady to promote like this.  But it fit things being kind of "off" here all around.

EATS
Looking over the big, two sided, laminated dinner menu we decided we'd pass (hot rock cooked steak, bbq chicken pasta...dated), order the table-side guacamole in the bar with our drink and move on.

The schtick of table-side guac seems a relic of 2000's.  Like flaming cherries jubilee table-side was for  the 1970's.  But Barbacoa sells a lot of guacamole this way.  As many as three guys with guac carts work on busy nights making up to 40 orders each we learned.  Shtick sells. (PS - There is a tip jar on the cart to tip the maker.)  Whether made table-side or in the kitchen doesn't matter as long as the guacamole is good.  And this, made and served in a molecajete, was good.  

THIS N THAT:

1) PARKING:  Private lot and it was pretty full.  Goes to show, I guess, we are in the minority opinion about Barbacoa's mediocrity.

2) ACCESSIBILITY:  Troublesome.  My Yelp friends who use wheelchairs will understand how dangerous it is to have wheelchair users have to travel behind parked cars against traffic in a parking lot  because the building owners violate the 24 year old Federal Civil Rights law and Idaho Code to put curb cuts at ADA parking locations  Also only one table at standard height in bar.  All other seating requires step up.  Dining room is step down on one side but ramp in on another.

3) NEIGHBORS:  Boise Park owned lake and walking path right behind Barbacoa.  Fast food restaurant to front.

Definitely go find this hidden gem in the Eldorado, right across from Brew Brothers! 

Hidden Pizza is an awesome by-the-slice pizza place. Personally I think it's the best grab-and-go food place at The Row.

You can definitely add toppings to any pizza if you're so inclined. They generally always have pepperoni, cheese, and meat lovers. They also have a rotating specialty pizza like Hawaiian and veggie. Both of these are also good if you're in the mood for pineapple on your pizza or a white sauce based one respectively. 

After you've chosen your pizza they'll heat it up in the firebrick oven and have it out in a few minutes. 

Now my favorite part: the shakers. They have several herbs/spices you can add like Parmesan and red pepper flakes, but I like to add the crushed garlic. So good! 

Keep in mind that they don't open until 5pm, but they are open late. A great place for a late night snack when you're enjoying a night out. The only downside is they can get a busy and if they run out of anything it does take a little while for them to make more.

Unfortunately, when we went to leave everything went downhill. My boyfriend and I decided before the night to take a cab home and had hitched a ride to the casino with family who were spending the night at the hotel. 

At around 2 a.m., we asked a security guard where the cabs were. She said she would call for one and it would be about 15 minutes. She said we had to wait outside otherwise we might lose our cab. We also called Discount Cab just to be safe. Discount couldn't give us an estimated time frame, but we figured the hotel had taken care of things.

40 minutes later, my we followed up with a different security guard . He had no update but said he saw a guy wait for over 90 minutes the other night. Great. Obviously the hotel knows they have a problem with cabs and have done nothing about it.

At around 3:00 a.m., we spoke to another security guard who was of no help. At 3:30 a.m., a VIP Taxi pulled up. My boyfriend and I tried to get in, but the driver informed us he was there to pick up an employee.

We then spoke with the security guard as to how we were unable to get a cab after 2 hours, but an employee could get one in 10 minutes. The security guard was rude and told us we should get over it.

Finally, around 4:10 a.m., the Discount cab that WE called arrived to picked us up.

The hotel's response also left something to be desired. I sent the casino a message on their website the following day detailing the incident and got no response. A week and a half later, I found an email to the customer service group and re-sent my response. 4 days later I got a response from customer service saying they were investigating the matter and would get back to me when they had finished the investigation.

I emailed them back today, 10 days after they said they were investigating. They responded that they did investigate, the Security Department took appropriate action, and they are looking into cab options. I'm glad they finally got around to looking into things, but it stinks that I had to be the one to follow-up. Also, how does a casino just now start looking into cab options when they are already an established business?

I will probably be back to Casino Del Sol because I had fun on both my visits. In the future though, I will not be drinking, and I'm certainly not taking a cab!

Having read all of the wonderful reviews, I was excited about going to Arnaud's this past weekend to celebrate a friend's birthday.  Unfortunately, the food was terrible and not worth the expensive price tag:
-The endive salad sounded wonderful, but it was essentially a messy plate of bland coleslaw.  The "dressing" had absolutely no flavor (definitely not the lemon vinagairette described), the endives were shredded into uneven pieces, and the blue cheese was crumbled into insanely large chunks.  (My friends got the caesar, which was standard.)
-The oysters were terrible!  Per the waiter's recommendation (and yelp reviews), I ordered the Oyster's Bienville.  They were super heavy and overcooked.  The oysters themselves were shriveled and chewy, and were covered with greasy stuffing (probably twice as much stuffing as oyster), which were then covered with a piece of melted cheese.  Melted cheese with oysters?  Umm... really?  The description itself said that the oysters were served with mushrooms, onions, and seasonings, and then topped with a white wine sauce.  Stovetop stuffing and cheese were NOT on the description.
-The chicken dish was okay... nothing spectacular.
-The gumbo was watery and bland.
-The vegetables (green beans and asparagus) were cold and covered congealed mystery sauce.

I stumbled across CRAVE Ice Cream Social during yesterday's excursion to the land of "I Have more money than I know what to do with!," or Geist, as most people call it. CRAVE is a relatively new shop having opened on 10/28/16, which doesn't seem like the ideal time to open up an ice cream shop almost directly alongside a large body of water. 

But hey, I suppose that gives them a few months to really get things together in anticipation of the summer lovin' that this place is bound to experience. 

I tend to like it when local businesses support other local businesses. This is the case with CRAVE, which sources their ice cream from a small batch shop in Anderson, sources their coffees/teas from nearby Noble Coffee & Tea Company and sources their pastries from Rosie's in Noblesville. The shop is located in a small strip area that houses Puccini's, a local bar and grill, some small/customized offices and a couple other businesses. It's right next to Geist Marina on the west side of the Fall Creek bridge. It's an inviting little place, a warm interior matched by an employee who was inviting, hospitable and was rushing to the door when she saw my plans to enter in a wheelchair. As you enter, a few tables are to the left and the ordering counter is straight ahead with 24 flavors of premium ice cream ready for tasting. They will let you sample their flavors. I ended up going with an old favorite - cookies n' cream. Pricing starts at what they called a kid's size at $3.25 - my guess is this size would suffice for many. When I initially said "a scoop," she reached for the kid's size - I upgraded it to the small for $4.50 plus tax. I'm guessing it was the equivalent of a two scoop serving. The ice cream was super creamy, perhaps a bit lighter on the "cookies" part than I would have liked but I also noticed that the ingredients are much finer than one might usually expect. That said, it was VERY good and definitely didn't have the processed feeling one gets from the larger shops.The coloring, while a tad different than some ice cream shops, is actually indicative of a more naturally made ice cream. 

While not everyone likes ice cream during the winter, I tend to think it's important to support shops like this one during their "off season" and I make an effort to visit. You can kinda sorta see Geist Reservoir from their shop and the entire area is pretty beautiful. I was genuinely impressed with the friendly customer service. Once I'd ordered the ice cream, she made an effort to move a chair from a table so I could sit there and enjoy it. They have one television that's on, but the environment is simply very relaxed with a few tables indoors and a couple spots outside available during the warmer months. As I noted in another review, there's a curb cut in the middle of the building - a little bit of an odd choice considering the ADA parking spots are to the left and right of this area. 

CRAVE is open seven days a week. While I wouldn't call it a destination ice cream shop, for any of Indy's Northsiders it's certainly worth the jaunt. I didn't try the coffees or pastries on this visit, but will certainly do so in the near future.

text:
Come for the side dishes and take them to your favorite good BBQ joint.

Many times you find a BBQ joint that has amazing BBQ and poorly executed sides that are almost an after thought.  All I can say is that Salt + Smoke should quit making BBQ and just make their business supplying side dishes to the many better BBQ places in the St. Louis area.

It started off pleasantly with a crowded house and expecting a wait, but the front of house staff was nice enough to push two tables together to sit my wife and sons and I almost immediately on a dinner night out to celebrate their end of school year.  We ordered a fairly simple selection of two burnt end brisket sandwiches, one double cheese burger with bacon, and a fish sandwich along with an appetizer of their fried brisket ravioli. 

The first clue that the night wasnt going to go well was when I asked my son how he wanted his burger and the waiter said that they only cook burgers one way and thats medium well.  Not sure how you can run a BBQ joint and not offer burgers cooked to order temp wise.  The rest of the order was straight forward with nothing customized or altered from their menu.  The wife ordered a Moscow Mule for a drink and I ordered a simple scotch.  

We ended up waiting a fairly good amount of time for the appetizer to come out.  The filing was dry and lacked any sauce and the dough was too thick which lead to a taste that was doughy more than anything else.  No flavor of the brisket came through, and the parsley sprinkled on top was tossed with what we originally thought was parmesan cheese but turned out to be what tasted like finely diced raw garlic.  

Before we each finished one ravioli the rest of the meal was served, which makes me wonder if the food was left at the counter sitting before it came to us as the difference in time between getting the appetizer and then the main dishes was vastly different.  The brisket on my order was cold lacking any cooking temperature what so ever, and my sons burger was well beyond medium well and the cheese on it was cool and hardening.  The wife said her fish was good but nothing special.

The only real good thing across all four dinner plates was the side dishes.  The slaw that the wife and I had was very tasty and had full thin slices of apple that really help the overall flavor.  The boys had white cheddar mac and cheese that was cooked nicely and had a wonderful flavor that when accented with a dash of pepper was even better.  

Since its not really a bar I wont spend much time on this one, but any place that serves a Moscow Mule in a plain glass should have their liquor license revoked.  Enough said there.

Salt + Smoke produced some great side dishes and some great sauces and I would gladly have them supply condiments to any BBQ joint in St. Louis, but outside of that the rest of the meal feel flat and was greatly a disappointment for the price.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The models (BERT, LR, SVM, NB) are in agreement with a low confidence, indicating a mixed review with a negative overall sentiment. The reviewer praises the side dishes but criticizes the main courses and service.

While Mulate's New Orleans is the original Cajun restaurant in New Orleans, the prices sure is a turn off, but as a tourist, it's what the city of New Orleans is known for. I hate being the first to write a review and it not being a great one, but it's coming. 

I have gone to the Aveda Institute in Castleton for a couple years now and have had great luck with the rate of mistakes being about the same as any other salon, one ever at Aveda.  On this occasion I went to Empire because its much closer to my house, cheaper, and apparently Aveda's phones just weren't working. I regret my decision and should have just waited. 

First, I called ahead to see if I had to make an appointment and told I could do walk-in until 2pm. I showed up around 1:15 and was told I "might" get in and apparently it was a big issue but never given a yes or no, just that the students were at lunch and she had no idea who would be free. I waited about 8-10 minutes and was finally called back. 

Now I know it's unfair to compare one place so much to another in a review, but I just had high expectations by comparison. Normally at Aveda an instructor would come by to talk to me about what I want after the student does to make sure they are on target. This never happened and the student just got to cutting after she understood what I wanted. This didn't seem too alarming until I found out that she's only being cutting for a couple of weeks and didn't know how to do some basic ideas. Not too horrible, since where it really went wrong was with the instructor. 

The instructor, Karma, never asked what I wanted and just started to "correct" everything, which is normal, until I realized that the whole inch/trim that I wanted became more like 2-2.5 inches before I knew it. Karma told the student to not be afraid to cut, even when she didn't know how much to cut. After I said I just wanted a trim, just shorten what I already had. Karma never asked for more details and by the time she asked the student, she already chopped it off. The one thing I was avoiding was chin-length hair, and that's what I now have. But the issues don't end there, Karma then made the sides uneven, the student did the length I wanted on one side, but Karma chopped that off too. I later found that they were left uneven even after I clearly stated that I did not want uneven sides and I am not interested in that trend. While, yes, the back is nicely blended (by the student) but it's waaaaay shorter than I wanted. I have lots of stray hairs that were missed, had to correct one side myself, never had the point cut that I wanted, and my birthday is in 5 weeks, a big birthday. I'm pissed. I didn't know that just shortening everything by one inch was so complicated!

Yes, you can ask "what did I expect? It's students." And I agree, but history showed much better professionalism from instructors in general, why should I expect anything less at Empire? Now I will stick to where I am comfortable, where I'm listened to and in the same 1.5 hours my simple trim took at Empire, would have included a scalp and chair massage and mini facial at Aveda. I now have choppy hair that is way too short that I never wanted. To make matters worse were the behavior of the students. One male students had droopy pants, another was busy picking at her belly button staring into space, another acted like the clippers she used on a male customer were a toy, and I kept smelling BO from somewhere. Topping it off was two students complaining about being written up for behavior. I wonder why? I thought they were taught professionalism! 

This is a long-winded review, I know.  But, if you want to save some money and try a school, go to Aveda where they have more class time before floor time and much more checks by the instructor. You spend a bit more ($17 compared to $8), but it's way worth it and the drive. Empire is really good for guys with simple cuts or women with long hair okay with getting an incorrect length cut off, or if you really don't know the length of an inch. My husband might still try out Empire, but clippers are harder to mess up, right? I sure hope so. Schools aren't the worst idea for a decent cut, I'm just shocked how so many horrible things happened in this one trip. I really could keep going into more detail, but I just don't have the time. I'm just glad hair grows back, I just wish it were faster. Approach with caution and don't be afraid to speak up and listen. It's your hair after all.

For those that don't know (since the AYCE menu doesn't show up on their website), it includes about 15 appetizers (pork katsu, shumai, miso, gyoza, sashimi, seaweed salad, spring roll, etc), 8 of their special rolls (plus another 8-10 that you pay an additional $2.50 for), pretty much all of their standard maki rolls, most of their nigiri, and about 10 of their hand rolls.  Plus a $6 wine and $6 large hot/cold house sake options which is pretty good.  

The food itself was very good!  We ordered the sashimi, gyoza, katsu, seaweed salad, shumai, and miso appetizers and everyone enjoyed theirs, especially the seaweed salad.  As for the sushi, it was also quite good, not too much rice on the nigiri, which had amply-sized pieces of fish.  The rolls were very tasty as well, both standard rolls like salmon avocado, as well as their special rolls.  I was very satisfied overall and didn't have one single item I didn't enjoy.

One gripe I had was the wait time after ordering.  They only had two sushi chefs on hand when I was there, which seemed under staffed given the large number of people there that night.  It is nice to know your sushi is freshly made, but our first course took about 35 minutes, and when we ordered a second round, it took them about 45 minutes.  All in all, it took about 2.5 hours from sitting down to signing the bill.  One other small issue I had was that I ordered sake at the beginning but it took several reminders for the waitress to finally bring it, but it was very good once it arrived.

Overall though, I would highly suggest this restaurant to anyone interested in AYCE sushi, but suggest they order a lot on the first go-around so they don't have to order a second time.

Tonight for example I ordered a Classic Ham Hoagie, with light mayo, lettuce and tomatoes.  That's as basic as it gets.  My ticket number was 70, and I went around the store and grabbed a bag of chips to go with my hoagie.   The wait time in line was unusually long, but it seemed the cashier was assisting another cashier with a problem, so it wasn't a big deal at all.   So after I pay I go and wait for them to call my number so I can pick up my sandwich and leave.  As I'm standing there I hear them call 69, 71 and then I see one of the associates having a conversation with some friends who stopped in.  She was working as she was talking.  Then I see the other associate begin making my sandwich.  That was 11 minutes after I placed the order for them to even start making it.    When I arrived home a few minutes later the hoagie wasn't wrapped properly and it opened up.  The only problem I had with the sandwich is the same issue I have with every Wawa, and it's that none of them understand what light mayo means. It used to be a helpful option so that I wasn't gagging on it, but now it just seems all Wawa's ignore this request.  The best part about this particular store is that it's soda fountain has chocolate and cherry you can add to it, and it's a great idea, and I've noticed it popping up in a few other of the new ones since.

text:
I RARELY (if ever) give out 5 star reviews, so those who regularly read them know this is a pretty big deal. 

This place is very small, with maybe a dozen or so tables - very Philly BYOB. It's decorated minimally, but enough where the slight authentic Italian touches are noticeable, such as the somewhat exposed kitchen, rustic signs, and giant espresso machine. The tables are bare with the simple candle and glasses decorating them - this place lets the food decorate the table, not a fancy cloth. It is all breathed over by a not too bright, not too dark light that allows you to read the menu without chancing a fire via proximity to candle but dim enough so your sunglasses can remain unworn, even at night! It's quite loud in the place, given the life coming from the kitchen and the seemingly always crowded tables inches of each other enjoying conversation, but somehow people in are still audible when speaking to you - good acoustics indeed.

The menu is large enough where there is variety, yet small enough where you cannot mistake the place for a chain restaurant with too large a menu. What I liked about it, and while there were many, they did not seem to follow the whole traditional Neopolitan red sauce model that seems to have populated the menus of many of Philadelphia's Italian eateries.  They had for us a basket of bread with a very tasty garlic infused olive oil that could have been a meal in itself. The bread was very flavorful, if not traditional Philadelphian Italian and went perfectly with the large, spreadable chunks of garlic that have been soaking in oil for the perfect amount of time. 

For an appetizer, we ordered the arugula salad special. It was certainly a portion fit for more than 1, definitely for 2, maybe 3. It had very bright greens, and prosciutto diced small enough where you could take a few pieces in at once, but large enough where, if a piece was consumed, it did not overwhelm, but rather complimented the greens and the cheese, a sharp provolone that again, complimented both in color and in taste - a Reggiano would have been too sharp. It was all lightly tossed in a subtle vinegar and oil dressing that again, complimented but did not overpower. 
Main course saw us both getting pasta - I ordered the fettuccine special, with a light yet flavorful red gravy served with Italian sausage, and my date ordered the gnocchi, again in a ragu. My fettuccine was cooked PERFECTLY - a perfect al dente. The gravy was a beautiful color; a nice red with some small yet delectable chunks of sausage and beef.  My date's gnocchi was possibly the best I've ever tried - well cooked, in perfectly sized bites, and in a ragu that put others to shame. It was light enough where you didn't hate yourself afterwards, but filling enough so you know that you just had a damn good ragu. The portions for both were large - almost too large, but when you have good food like that, it's nice to see a large portion so you get to relive the experience the next day. 
For dessert we split their home made Tira Misu. Very light, well portioned, and flavorful, you could taste the coffee, chocolate, and creme in each bite. It was enough for two people to enjoy and to round out a great meal. They also serve espresso which, while nothing to really write home about, was not bad and definitely was the real deal.  

The service was good - our waiter was prompt without being annoying and was able to provide recommendations as well as take orders from memory, an increasing rarity. I did, however, have a few gripes. For service, there seemed to be different people bringing out our food at different times, rather than having the same server throughout our meal. One server should be it, maybe a food runner or another to drop off something, but one person takes the orders. Along with this, while they opened our wine, they did not pour, and they did not serve our red with proper wine glasses, but rather a white wine glass, though this is me getting nitpicky. Finally, they did not seem to have a proper hostess - it seemed to be whoever was closest to the door at the time, or the owner, so one may have waited by the door for a while before being helped. 

I'd recommend making reservations - I called (they aren't on Open Table) well over 24 hours in advance and they only had one table open at 8:30.

All in all Giorgio was a very enjoyable experience that I hope many will share and enjoy. I'd also like to save the best for last - our entire meal, appetizer to dessert, was only $58, so definitely take the time to try this little BYOB out - you won't be disappointed.

text:
Came here with my management team to celebrate ten years in business (night two of a three day celebration.) we came because here were tons of vegan options, including vegan cheeses and toppings - and we have a bunch of veggie eaters and vegans in our party. Let's talk about the pizza, pretty good, Neapolitan style, with the added benefit of not having to be in the dumpster fire that is Naples. The food came out quickly, which was a true mercy (so we could get out sooner). The vegans were all super happy with their food as well!

I hate to leave a review like this, because it's not really about the restaurant, but the night was just ruined by management's choices. 

In fairness, they did call me earlier in the day and say "we're going to have a band tonight, is that ok?" I did ask if it was going to be a concert style thing, or like a chill jazz band type thing, and I was told that they didn't really know, but how loud could it be considering it's a pizza place in a mall? How BAD could it be?

Really bloody bad as it turns out. This is a fairly post-modern, open style restaurant, with exposed ceilings and concrete floors. Acoustically it's probably be a tough venue to start with, but add the 110 decibel Casio keyboards, pseudo-rock guitar, and the yelling of the patrons to try and be heard by their table mates, it became a  cacophony.

I guess the loudness didn't bother too many other guests, they probably turned their hearing aids down. As a group of diners ranging from their forties to their twenties, we were the youngest customers in the entire place who weren't there with their grandchildren.

Not only was the band so loud that literally no one could hear anything (not even a waiter YELLING in your ear), but the quality and song selection was that of your average night at an open mic karaoke bar in a Chinese restaurant. It was just so weird... who was the audience? Where did all these old people come from? Do they know Pharrell's catalog? Are there a lot of John Legend fans in exclusively white, retirement homes?

The waiters did apologize for it, the bar tender actually swore and said "this is f...ing ridiculous" and the staff seemed genuinely embarrassed about the fiasco. We got our wine comped even though we didn't complain - it was that bad! 

I think this is probably a good place for lunch or dinner when there isn't a band. But it was literally a painful experience that damaged ear drums, completely destroyed even the possibility of conversation, and ruined dinner.

Let us know when band nights are rethought - we might be back.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The models show moderate agreement on a low rating, with BERT and SVM leaning towards a 3-star rating, but the overall sentiment of the review is overwhelmingly negative due to the loud band, which outweighs the positive comments about the food and service.

Bourbon Street for sure is a must see when you visit New Orleans but be aware that you will most definitely will see a whole bunch of "oh shit, did you see that?" going on!! ;)

I do agree with some of the previous reviews left that there is a different vibe going on during that day versus the night time Bourbon Street & to be honest I would not bring young kids to Bourbon Street at night at all! 

Bourbon Street is like no there place around...you'll see LOTS of people from all over & there are lots of clubs to go to & of course many places to buy alcohol from since it is legal to carry/ drink alcohol in the streets in Louisiana as long as it's in a plastic container..which I have to admit is pretty cool to do :)...alcohol to go..oh yea, baby!! 

Bourbon Street for sure will shock you if it's your 1st time visiting..1st of all depending on the time of day you visit there's a smell that hits your nostrils that is a combination of urine & nasty sh$t but then you'll be shocked visually by seeing the huge XXX Hustlers signs/posters posted up outside of Hustlers on Bourbon Street...( you should have seen my hubby the 1st time we went to Bourbon & saw the Hustlers signs..poor thing was so confused..should I look or not?!! ;)))))))) it was hilarious! 

NOW, having just described the above to you please don't be deterred from visiting Bourbon Street because amongst those damn freaky, freaky places there are some AWESOME & "speak to my soul" live music clubs on Bourbon Street that play jazz & zydeco that you have to experience at least once in your lifetime.

And there are also quite a few yummy food places on or near Bourbon Street (Oceana Grill being one of those places) & Bourbon Street normally is where you will get to see a lot of the NOLA street performers...from tap dancers to drummers using nothing but a bucket & drumsticks..now that's talent!! 

Last piece of advice.. just be safe & be aware of your surroundings when visiting Bourbon Street & just use common sense so you can fully enjoy & experience the famous Bourbon Street!

Side-note: As of 7/29/2017 there is construction being done to portions of Bourbon Street right down the middle of the street & it sucks!! Looks like construction is going on until the end of 2017. 

-Rebecca out

text:
I can't believe how many people on here are griping about Casa Video's late fees. Seriously? They charge you $.99 a day (might be more for new releases). Blockbuster used to claim your firstborn child if you returned a movie late. Casa's just extending your rental period for a slightly higher price. If you really truly cannot remember to return videos for weeks at a time, then please, I beg you, go to Netflix. I don't want you disappearing for two months with the movie I want to rent.

As for Casa Video itself, this is the best video store I've ever been to, and I've been to some great video stores. If it's available on DVD, they generally have it on DVD, and if it's not, they have it on VHS. The few times I couldn't find a movie, I asked at the front desk and discovered I'd been looking in the wrong section. For the most part the employees know right where everything is, which is mind-blowing considering the number of movies they have. And, while the hyper-organized nature of the place can be a little disorienting, it's nice to be able to browse the "Giant Monsters" section. Or the "Derek Jarmin"section. Or the "Documentaries Addressing Social Issues" section. You could have a pretty amazing scavenger hunt without leaving the store.

What else.... The DVDs are generally in good condition. The employees are all helpful, kind movie nerds. There's an unexpectedly vast soda selection. And free popcorn. And a video game section. And a porn section. They're open until 1am, and you can return movies right up until then on the day they're due. There's an after-hours drop box. There's some kind of rent-by-mail program, which I've never tried. And they link your account to your driver's license, instead of giving you another card to carry around.

All told, Casa Video is one of the best businesses in Tucson, and one of the best video stores in the country. We're lucky to have it.

This review is based on my most recent/second trip to Mama Campisi's - July 4, 2010.  I did go a few years back and remembered really liking it but not much else.

My husband and I took my out of town in-laws for their first Hill experience after an afternoon at the Science Center.  I should have thought first and realized it was a Sunday and that nothing would be open.  That's how we ended up here.

Though there seemed to be plenty of room upstairs, we got seated downstairs, where the ambience is quite different - in a bad way.  Should have known after having to go down a rather dimly lit flight of stairs.  Glad we survived the journey.

Service, in general, was slow.  The girl that was in charge of refilling drinks and bringing us bread was really scatter brained.  The knife at my place was filthy but quickly replaced when question was raised.

After a long wait, we started with the toasted raviolis - ya know, to give my in-laws the true STL experience.  They were pretty tasty.  I've never had the "original" style toasted ravs.  Different, but I'd eat them again for sure.

After another long wait, we got out meals.  I got the Mama's Trio - nothing to write home about.  I would have been just as pleased - maybe more so - at the Old Spaghetti Factory.  My husband got the Veal Spiedini which was pretty good, but being a provel lover, how could a piece of meat smothered in provel not taste good?  He did comment that it was chewier than expected at times.  His parents got the Linguine Salsiccia and Baked Beef Ravioli.  They seemed to enjoy both.

At this point, I would have maybe gone for 2 or 3 stars, but then there was Keith.

First upstairs and then down with us, Keith stumbles down the stairs to interrupt everyone's dinner exclaiming how 4th of July is his favorite holiday, how glad he was we were here, etc.  Ok...maybe Keith is some strange owner or manager...?  We indulge him.  Then he badgers everyone into singing along to "God Bless America".  Most people continue to indulge him while I giggle.  He stops in the middle of singing to look at me and exclaim "Don't laugh.  It's not funny!"  Well, it's not anymore.  He did apologize for disrespecting me after the song was over, but the damage was done.  Oh, and Keith isn't a manager or something.  He just some random Sunday regular, as was told while laughing it off by our waitress.  

I wouldn't normally judge a restaurant by the other guests, but the fact that the waitresses blew it off like it was nothing instead of apologizing and that they didn't stop him after doing it first upstairs really peeves me.  It really ruined my meal, and I will NOT return as a result.  Thanks, Keith.

Location
Located in a shopping strip all the way to the left next to Reyta Filipino restaurant. Long hallway walking in. Sign your waiver as directed and pay for what you want at the front desk! I've previously eaten here with decent experiences. During the COVID-19 pandemic, my husband & I have ordered delivery from them multiple times and have been satisfied with their quality of food. However I will never order or visit their establishment again after the take-out order experience I had last night. I had ordered a salad with grilled shrimp- this was my entire dinner. The other items ordered were for my husband. The restaurant called me to state the online delivery service had incorrect information and shrimp was not an option. I told them to go ahead & make the salad without the protein. I contacted the online delivery service and spent a good 15 minutes ensuring that they were to only deduct the shrimp from the salad but keep the salad. After all, it was the only item for my dinner. Sad I didn't get a protein for dinner (I am a pescatarian) but not the end of the world. At least I had a meal coming. 

Of course, the food was delivered without the salad. My entree. I contacted the online delivery service which was another disaster, but I then called the restaurant to try to rectify directly. The man who answered raised his voice & responded to me yelling at me that did I realize I was yelling over JUST A SALAD?? I do admit I was raising my voice. I was hungry and had spent an hour waiting on delivery for a dinner that never came so of course I was upset. He went on admonishing me- that "there were bigger things to worry about than JUST A SALAD" and again yelled that did I realize I was yelling about "JUST A SALAD??" 

The restaurant business should NEVER respond to a customer in this manner. I've been in the business myself. Furthermore my JUST A SALAD was my DINNER. My ENTIRE DINNER. I spent most of my younger life justifying that I was worthy enough to eat, that I deserved to put food in my body, and trying to shrug off all the social norms that are placed on women as to what is acceptable regarding food, body image, et cetera- and to have this man reinforce that I was NOT EVEN worthy of having JUST a salad, JUST my dinner, is completely unacceptable. Yes, I know there are worse things in the world- coronavirus pandemics, violence, murder, poverty, people who haven't eaten for days or weeks. I get it. But this man was not in charge of those concerns in his job. His job was to deliver the food people ordered. Not berate them and tell them there were bigger concerns in life than them getting a dinner they paid for. 

I refuse to conduct business with this restaurant ever again. Shame on that man.

text:
Flying Pie marked its return to Broadway Avenue with the opening of their new store at the former Buster's location. For years, Flying Pie operated a hole-in-the-wall shop next to the Suds Tavern. They left that location after they were evicted due to someone buying out most of the businesses along that strip just down from Boise State University. That company's plans were disrupted when it turned out Cobby's had a long-term lease and they weren't able to get that last building. Meanwhile, Flying Pie had gone and was later replaced by the Pie Hole.

The Buster's location gives the Pie a lot more room inside -- room for at least 100 diners -- and they've added an outdoor seating area, a first for the Flying Pie. There's even an outdoor standup counter. 

The Pie hosted a soft opening Sunday (ahead of their 3 p.m. Tuesday grand opening) as a benefit with the $10 cost donated to the Life's Kitchen program, which teaches culinary and life skills to at-youth risk. That program does a wonderful job.

During three serving times, each accommodating 100 diners, Flying Pie debuted a new personal size lunch pizza with a thin artisan crust. I found the crust superior to their regular dough. It had a lighter, crisper texture.

There were also new pizza offerings, including a Thai chicken and an El Diablo, with Basque chorizo and Cajun andouille sausage and a habanero sauce. Both were excellent, along with a roasted mushroom pizza. 

The building is unlike any of the Pie's other Boise and Meridian locations. it has an industrial look, with lots of stainless steel and even a roll-up garage door that I imagine will come open when the weather warms up. Also new for the Flying Pie is an outdoor seating area and a stand-up bar with a fire pit over the edge of the counter.

The downside will be parking. There's limited lot parking and nearby businesses and apartments have signs telling customers of the former Buster's at that location not to park in their lots.

This location looks like a winner. Welcome back to Broadway Avenue. You've been gone too long.

I returned for lunch two days after the official opening and had one of their artisan pizzas, which I learned will only be served at the Broadway location. I ordered the Carnivore, with red sauce, pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage, linguica, mushrooms, red peppers & sliced red onions on the artisan thin crust.

The pizza was great. I didn't realize they were offering table service at this location. No more listening for your name to be called and going to the counter. They also brought metal silverware wrapped in a napkin and at least two employees walked the floor, talking with diners and asking whether they were enjoying their meal.

The Broadway store is using a gas oven, different from the electric ovens used by the other locations. It fires hotter and cooks the pizzas quicker.

I downgraded my rating after a disappointing lunch experience. I ordered a Carnivore on the thin crust exclusive to the Broadway store. 

When the pizza arrived, it was lukewarm. That meant one thing: It came out of the oven and then sat forgotten for 10 minutes before it was brought to my table. That's the only explanation I could fathom.

The temperature was more like it would be if you had a few pieces left over at the end of the meal, not at the beginning.

It was funny, too, that the server brought a spatula but no plate. It would have been easy enough to get up and ask for one. Instead, I used the spatula to move pieces from one side of the serving pan to the other. Sometimes, you just have to laugh at the absurdness of it all.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The review text is overwhelmingly positive, with the reviewer praising the new location's amenities, menu offerings, and service. While there is a negative experience described in the review, it is isolated to a single visit and does not seem to be a systemic issue. Model predictions show moderate agreement on a lower rating, but BERT's prediction of 4 stars is the most confident and aligns with the overall tone of the review.

I love Korean food and my bosses know it, so when I had a business trip they told me to stop here. 

I got the bibimbap, not dolsot, just in a regular bowl and it was okay. The vegetables seemed fresh and there was a good variety, it was a better selection than some other Korean restaurants I've been to. Rice was cooked well, not crispy but not soggy. But, the beef was ground beef, which I've had before in bibimbap, but the seasoning on it, I hadn't. I didn't care for it, it tasted almost like breakfast sausage and I couldn't mask it even with all the gochujang that I put on.

The banchan was okay, basic cabbage kimchi, cucumber kimchi, radish, and bean sprouts. Radish and bean sprouts were fresh and tasted good, cucumber kimchi had good flavor and heat, but the cabbage kimchi was older and sour.

My girlfriend got the fried chicken, not realizing what it was, but wondering why it was so expensive. There is no rice or anything served with the chicken but it's $17 still, and that's because of how many you get. I didn't count how much chicken there was, but it looked like a small mountain on the plate and it was served right out of the fryer. The flavor was okay, it tasted like rice flour with minimal seasoning, and I figure that's because they use the same chicken to put sauce on for other dishes. 

All in all, it was an okay place, not the best nor the worst Korean restaurant I've been to.

I have taken 2 classes at lithe and have mixed feelings about the classes. On one hand, I like that form was emphasized and a lot of exercise was focused on core stabilization. I felt that the instructers were energetic and attentive. The facility was clean and modern as well. 

My first critique is the language and descriptions used on the website. One class is described as helping you "return to your 23 inch waist." This is an unhealthy (http://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/educational/lose_wt/risk.htm) and unrealistic expectation that should never be advocated for by fitness professionals. A healthy waist size for an adult woman should be less than half her height, which means a 23 inch waist would be appropriate for someone roughly 4 feet tall. Another ridiculous claim I saw was that a certain class would help to "re-texturize" your skin tone. Though exercise in general may help to give skin a younger appearance, it's irresponsible to claim that one of their classes will specifically re-texturize skin. There are so many well documented reasons to exercise, that there should be no reason to make false claims. I also think the language that is used in the descriptions of the class are condescending to women. As a place that seemingly is all about strengthening and uplifting women, naming classes "high mini" and "skinny jeans" seems contradictory. Also, renaming classic exercise moves such as a heel raise to "stiletto" is another example of the condescending language that doesn't sit well with me. Clearly, this place is targeting adult professional women (at least the price tag would imply this). I have exercised my entire life and teach exercise as well. Women do not need their exercises renamed in order for them to understand them. Its exhausting to think that you have to re-learn another exercise dialect to feel comfortable in the class. As a female health profession, I find this language insulting. 

As for the classes, they were nice for light strengthening and core stability, but if you want a good sweaty cardiac workout, this place is not for you. I barely broke a sweat in both classes (one class was described as having a cardio component). Lithe might be ok as a supplement to a cardio routine, but for me, it does not fulfill all my exercise needs and is not a good value for the money.

text:
I've been to Nashville several times, including trips with each of my three kids individually on separate occasions (college visits, tagging along during conferences, etc.). It's the only place that has that distinction in our family history. The one place to which I have taken each of them without fail while there was the Hermitage. On our recent visit with my wife and grandson (who happens to be named Jackson, for no reason related to Andrew), our venture to the Hermitage was the fourth visit I have made to this enjoyable site.

A visit to the Hermitage can be dissected into five parts. The museum provides a great overview of the salient facts concerning Jackson and his times. The grounds facilitate an enjoyable fresh-air experience. The servant quarters provide insight into the slaveholding culture of the day and the microcosm of Jackson's participation in that institution. The gardens provide a more aesthetic aspect to the adventure. Within the gardens is also the family cemetery, providing additional pieces to the puzzle of Jackson's family history. Finally and foremost is the main house, which is unquestionably the highlight of a visit to the Hermitage. It's all extraordinarily interesting.

The museum itself is at the point of entry. It gives you the chance to establish a working knowledge about Jackson, his life, his family and those associated with him. What you see here will broaden and deepen the learning experience when touring the grounds. There was clearly a lot to admire about the man, but also a lot of things that cast him in a negative light. How you judge him, assuming you feel compelled to do so, depends on the weight you place on each of his respective actions and achievements, both positive and negative.

The grounds are amazing! Setting aside the historical significance of the place for a moment, if you are there on a nice weather day, just sitting outside and/or strolling the grounds can be an enjoyable experience by itself. I have been fortunate that each of my times here have been during beautiful autumn or winter weather, with crisp but moderate temperatures and copious sunshine. While such things are unfortunately out of our control, I can only say that the lovely weather has added greatly to my enjoyment during each visit.

The on-site historical re-creation is superb. The workers are "in the day" (i.e., they don't pretend to be living in the past while you observe and interact with them, such as they do at Plimouth Plantation, for example). But they are in period costume. On our last visit, we were able to observe the re-enactment of a duel. Learning about the ritual of dueling (and it truly was a ritual) provided a fascinating window through which to view an aspect of the culture of Jackson's time. Activities such as these add greatly to the enjoyment and learning experience of a visit to the Hermitage.

Roaming the grounds can be an eye-opening process. The slave quarters provide insight into the less discussed portion of the Hermitage's history. More recent interpretation among the documents in these buildings is quite illuminating and worthwhile.

The gardens are a nice diversion as well. Not only do they provide an aesthetic break, it is also there you'll find the tomb of Jackson, his wife Rachel and several family members. It provides a bit of insight into family history.

The house is the highlight of the tour. I'm a sucker for well-preserved historical houses, but the history associated with this one makes it particularly special. The furnishings are beautiful and the guides do a very good job with the interpretation of what you see when walking through.

In the end, it goes without saying that Jackson was a complicated man. His treatment of Native Americans as President and the fact that he owned a large number of slaves in his private life were two hugely negative scars on his legacy. Like physical scars, such character disfigurements can give someone an initial repulsive appearance. But it's only when we take a deep breath and adjust to that first impression that we can move past it to see someone like Jackson in totality; that is, with a rational eye. Once we see the good and the bad, we can synthesize an entire, often complex, picture. But good or bad, it's all history. The issues at hand do not constitute the man and the man is not the sole embodiment of those issues. This place helps a person to assimilate a collection of facts that are contributions to the aggregate that make up the mosaic of time.

text:
As much as I'd like to say that Brew Brothers was part of our plan all along, the truth is that we only really came here after our attempts to check out the vendors at Wing Fest failed pretty hard.  Still, despite how they may not have been our first choice, we were definitely grateful for them!  Considering how hungry we were, the minimal wait and the decent food were practically blessings!

Despite how they seem to sit on the Silver Legacy's side of the catwalk level, Brew Brothers is actually part of El Dorado.  Not that it matters much, since they're sister hotels (ditto for Circus Circus).  Rather, what does matter is the menu, which is actually kind of impressive.  Along with their half dozen or so house brews on tap, they have a nice mix of typical brewery eats (starters, salads, sandwiches, burgers, pizzas, BBQ, etc.).  Since we were torn on trying a burger or the pastrami sandwich, one of my friends and I ended up getting both to share.

-- CRISPY THICK CUT ONION RINGS with a Sri-Ranch-a Dip...$7.50
(https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/brew-brothers-reno-3?select=ki7utlJeZD-MyeN_kf1ihw)
I really wasn't expecting much, but this was actually pretty decent!  The breading wasn't too thick (or thin) and it had just the right amount of crunch to every bite.  Also, even though the onions themselves were a little dry, the dip helped a lot (plus, it had a nice, subtle kick to it).

-- BISON BURGER - Lean Ground Buffalo Patty, Green Leaf Lettuce, Tomato, Onion, Pickles, Mayo, and Choice of Cheese (Cheddar)...$11.75
(https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/brew-brothers-reno-3?select=ECScYDxRxT-PMeg80PCaDg)
As hefty as my first ever bison burger was, sadly, it didn't amaze.  While the overall taste of it was fine, the burger just wasn't as satisfying as I had hoped.  It wasn't shocking that it wasn't very juicy (bison is pretty lean), but I didn't expect it to be so crumbly either (just dry, not overcooked).  

-- HOT PASTRAMI PRETZEL ROLL - Thin Sliced Warmed Pastrami, Swiss Cheese, Pickles, and Whole Grain Mustard on a Toasted Pretzel Roll...$9.75
(https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/brew-brothers-reno-3?select=MUiujxuQT4qd_HwZ6x_Jrw)
The fries on the plate were great, but the pastrami sandwich was awesome!  The pretzel bun was terrific, there was lots of melted Swiss, and they didn't overdo it with the mustard.  That said, the pastrami was clearly the star; plentiful, juicy, tender, and very well seasoned.  So good!

Featuring DJ's and various bands on a nightly basis, Brew Brothers also doubles as a nightlife spot (the place is pretty big).  However, since we never passed by it that late at night, I can't say how busy they get.  If their drinks are as cheap as their house brews though (just $4 a pint!), they might not be a bad spot to sit and enjoy a round while listening to some live music.

All in all, based purely on the burger and onion rings, this would probably be a three star review.  However, between the pastrami sandwich and the cheap beers, it's an easy call to round up from THREE AND A HALF STARS.  I'm not sure if I'd ever make a point of eating at Brew Brothers again, but they're far better than some of the alternatives here.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The models show moderate agreement with a slight lean towards a higher rating, with BERT being the most confident. The review text highlights the positive aspects of the experience, including the decent food, minimal wait, and impressive menu.

text:
Indianapolis Motor Speedway Hall of Fame is somewhat disappointing do to complete lack of imagination.  If you are a huge fan of the Indy 500 and have followed all the race car drivers over the last 50 years this will be a meaningful stop for you regardless. 

There are many Indy winning cars on display here with a paragraph describing their unique qualities. One of them is number 32, the winner of the 1911 first Indianapolis race. There is a nearly exact replica this car at the Coker Tire Museum in Chattanooga Tennessee. The current special displays July 2018 are an homage to the Unser family. Most of the non-car displays are about trophies and winning. 

There is nearly no discussion of safety developments or even mortality on the track. In fact there is little engineering discussion whatsoever. Unless you count the almost insulting animation in the zone 4 room demonstrating what a 4-stroke engine cycle is. My thought is if you don't know what a four-stroke engine is already, you probably aren't that interested in racing and won't be in this museum.

Unlike many museums, there is very little effort to draw the non-enthusiast viewer into the topic. Unless you're already interested in race cars you'll probably think this is just another car showroom. There are so many missed opportunities!

For example they have a website QR code where you can listen to very brief audio by elderly race car drivers, but they really don't say much. For example they'll say this car had many superior advantages to the others and then end the topic right there. Leaves you hanging wondering:  What advantages? You feel like they don't trust you with the information and you probably wouldn't understand it anyway.

There were a total of 3 cutaway displays in the entire Museum. One was of a modern transaxle near the Indianapolis winning cars. There was also a partial cutaway of a formula car in the final room. Then there was a "petting zoo" for an engine where you could lift a crankshaft see what valves look like and View and touch an engine block.  

There was also a small tire display by a single Tire company that was up some interest because it showed the progressive changes in tires over the years.  Nothing about racing protective equipment, nothing about pit crews or how they work, nothing about racing technique, little said about car engineering and handling tuning, nothing about serious risks of driving 160 mph for 500 miles!

There was almost nothing exciting such as a discussion of why or how they designed the ground effects or tail Wings on these race cars.

in addition to the above, it might have been nice to have a better documentary movie about the track. The 8 minute movie in the theater was almost completely lacking in any interest or information. You could probably gather about the same amount of information by walking around the parking lot walking up the grassy knoll and looking down on the track yourself. And you can do that for free without going into the museum.
I suppose my expectations were higher. I was expecting possibly even some kind of driving simulator given the advanced technology of games and simulator cars these days. Nothing even close was found.

It's hard to say who the target audience is.  There is little of substance for adults and even less of interest to younger kids.

So if you want to see trophies and winning cars and a few paragraphs about the last five minutes of the race for the winning drivers this is your Museum. Otherwise just park in the center of the oval step out to the grassy knoll and gaze on  history.

On my first visit to Peg's, we were quickly seated in the busy diner. I was served a hot cop of joe and our waitress handed us our menus. After looking at all the Yelp pictures the night before, I went for "Peg's favorite breakfast", the Peg's Glorified Huevos Ranchero, a selection from their Monterey Skillet Breakfast. Each skillet is served with olden hash browns, pico de gallo, cabbage slaw, fresh pinto beans and warm tortillas. One word: delicious. It was everything I wanted and more. They even include a piece of fresh fruit, which I barely touched after finshing my skilled. 

On my most recent visit during Hot August Nights, I debated between the tamale & eggs skillet or the breakfast burrito skillet, and went with the latter. green chiles, cheddar and ranchero sauce. I was unsure how big this burrito was going to big considering how much food the skillet already is and I can safely say I had a hard time finishing my burrito. Not necessarily the best burrito, with a little too much egg, but overall, another fulfilling breakfast with great sides. 

Both times I've gone, I've been given great service. After a night of heavy drinking, a breakfast at Peg's is the perfect thing before hitting the pool and loading up with beers. Expect to spend $30 for two people including drinks. Food is great, staff is great, and prices are a little more than most diners, but you get tons of food, all of which is delicious. I may have just traded in my usual breakfast at Hash House for breakfast at Peg's.

text:
I'm not sure I've ever left a review on Yelp, but after my experience with Nashville 4D Baby, I felt compelled. 

My husband and I were elated when we found out we were expecting. I didn't think any part of me could wait until the anatomy scan at 20 weeks to find out the sex of our baby. Because I was so impatient and excited, I booked an elective ultrasound for the day I hit 15 weeks. We drove 1.5 hours to the West End office for our 11:30am appointment. We showed up at 11:20am and there was no one there. The doors were locked and it took 2 calls for anyone to answer the phone at the office. The girl on the other end of the line said the tech must be running late. No problem, we understand. Of course it was 27 degrees and snowing on that day, so we were stuck outside for 15 minutes waiting on the tech to show up. Finally, she pulls in and gets out of her car. We were standing on the front porch of the office and she didn't acknowledge us once. Not even a "Hi, how are you?" or "I'm so sorry I'm late!" Even after we got into the office she handed us a form to fill out without so much as a "Woo, it's cold out there, isn't it?" Nothing. At this point I was getting pretty annoyed at the lack of hospitality and kindness. Still, we spent a pretty penny in gas money just to get to the appointment, and I didn't want to leave empty handed. 

We headed into the ultrasound room and got down to business. After 5 or so minutes the tech finally warmed up to us a little bit and started showing at least a little bit of personality. We felt better about everything, and after we left we decided that maybe she was just frazzled from being late to work or something going on in her personal life. We were overjoyed to find out we were having a baby boy and we couldn't stop staring at the printouts of the scan. 

After getting home with our CD disc of images, we realized that our Apple computers couldn't open the discs. I tried on my iMac, our Mac Book Pro, and a friend's Mac Book. Nothing worked. It kept showing up as a "unreadable" disc. I gave 4D Baby a call and they were very kind in offering to send us another disc, free of charge. I waited for about one week and then the disc showed up. Same thing, unreadable. I gave them a call back and was met with "Well, maybe it's your computer" excuses. Well, if it were my computer then why did it do it on 3 different ones? (Come to find out sometimes PCs compress images on a CD in a way that Macs have a hard time reading - Understandable. And not their fault necessarily). 

The following weeks were back and forth phone calls between me and the 4D Baby offices. I didn't have access to anyone with a PC computer as all of our family and friends use Apple, so I asked if they could just email me the images that way I could have them (afterall, I did pay $100 to have the images) and they said sure. Days passed, then weeks. After them promising on multiple occasions to send the files and then to follow up with me, they never did. Now I'm 27 weeks pregnant and still never received the first digital photo of our baby at 15 weeks. It's frustrating to have waited this long and still get nothing, especially after paying what we did and driving as far as we had. 

Had it just been the lack of friendliness, or just the disc debacle, I probably would've let it go. But I feel disappointed with our experience with 4D Baby considering all of the above. We're hoping to do another ultrasound in the coming weeks to see the baby all filled out, and hopefully to get a face shot, but I won't be booking with this business. Despite being totally hormonal at this point, I'm certainly not an unreasonable customer in hoping that I'd actually get what I paid for. I'll give 2 stars simply because it was such a treat to know the sex 5 weeks early, but otherwise I'd give 1 star.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The customer's review expresses strong disappointment with their experience at 4D Baby, citing poor hospitality, technical issues, and unfulfilled promises. We purchased a used refrigerator/freezer (side by side). Six months later, it stopped cooling completely. We called our home warranty company who scheduled an appliance repair company to come and fix it. 

The repairman found that the compressor had been "rigged" by someone using poor wiring skills. He was able to repair it properly, removing the three bad devices used and replacing the three with one device. He did this in under an hour. 

We obviously can't be certain it was done by Bayshore Appliances, but you would think that they would check these units out thoroughly to make sure their customers aren't getting badly wired appliances that are most likely going to break down or burn out in a short period of time. We won't be purchasing from them again since this was either done by them or overlooked by them and could have cost us all of the foods in our refrigerator/freezer. Luckily, we caught it in time. We feel this was neglectful on their part.

Our lesson learned was that we should, if we need to purchase another used appliance in the future, ask to look at the back bottom of the unit and look at how the wiring looks. If it looks spliced up, ramshackle and "filthy"....it's most likely been rigged or abused.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The review expresses strong negative sentiment towards Bayshore Appliances due to a potentially rigged used appliance that stopped cooling. All models (BERT, LR, SVM, NB) agree on a low rating, with high confidence from BERT, supporting the final decision.
