Service: Waiters were extremely busy and had too many tables. The back of the menu detailed their training service, but I didn't see it. 

Food: Three courses once you order an entree, but my entire entree (Chicken Bern) was salty and the salad lackluster. A very intense number of steak options in terms of cuts, thickness, and portions. 

Atmosphere: Red lighting? Not reassuring for mealtime. The menu boasts a 1000(?) seat area for their wine selection, but waiters bumped my chair all night to take care of neighboring tables.

However! There is a room just for desserts-- but our meal was too expensive to even consider going to the dessert room. Everyone in our party was not impressed with their dinners, so I wouldn't recommend it. All hype, not better than your average dinner. Boca's isn't too far away, and I heard many good things about it! Try that instead, and save the cash for your ride home.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The review text expresses a negative sentiment, mentioning the high price and disappointing food. All models agree on a low rating, with BERT's high confidence supporting the decision.

text:
Decent. We arrived on a Sunday, first thing at opening. There was a group seated already, but other than that it was empty.  The server was sweet and attentive and we were brought water right away.  The specials were up on the board so as we perused the menu, we decided to start with an order of fried pickles and the prosciutto fries.  The pickles were great, long and thinly sliced, there was a nice ratio of breading to pickle.  The prosciutto fries were not at all like we had pictured from the description.  I don't know if we had more than 2 or 3 teeny pieces of prosciutto in the entire plate and they got cold and soggy so quickly that they became unappetizing.  

We were 2 adults and 2 kids (who are just as much foodies as their parents) so we decided on sharing 3 plates.  We ordered the Sweet Child of Mine burger cooked medium, the special flat bread and the Parma pizza.  The burger was the best of then 3, although it was definitely cooked more to medium well with a grey center.  The pizza was very greasy and there was so much arugula on it that as soon as you grabbed a slice, an entire salad fell off of it. Also, the chili on the flatbread over took much of the flavor that it was overpowering. It wasn't horrible, but honestly, the meal was just okay.  I did enjoy the fries that came with the burger. 

Overall, we might return to try some other things out, but a few of our picks were just not worth trying again.

text:
Luke's Lobster, the much touted and celebrated New York lobster roll company (by way of Maine) has finally arrived in Philadelphia, opening to much fanfare and praise.  It does have something that despite all the food options in Philly, the city had previously lacked: a good lobster roll at a good price.  If you are expecting something that resembles lobster salad with gobs of mayo, then Luke's Lobster is not for you. Otherwise, prepare to be delighted.

On opening day, I waited in a 20 minute line to get my hands on one of their famous rolls.  The lobster roll (for $15, or add chips and a drink for $2 more) comes chock full of fresh lobster claw and knuckle meat, overflowing out of a buttered and toasted New England style bun.  With just a hint of mayo to hold the meat in place, you can actually taste the lobster instead of the dressing.  Because this is real lobster meat, don't be alarmed if you find a bit of shell or cartilage in your food (as did I, and it ended up being my only gripe about the quality of the meat).  Because this is real lobster meat, the sandwich is short, but dense.  Savor it.  The menu also includes lower priced rolls with crab and shrimp, or if you're indecisive, a Taste of Maine ($20) gives you half a roll of each variety with chips and drink.

The space is completely different from the previous tenant (Bonte), with a New England crab shack feel.  The staff is young and friendly, and I liked the fact that all their chips and soda come from New England (Cape Cod chips and Maine Root soda).  I question whether or not Philadelphia can really support an "everyman" Lobster Roll place, because at $15 per roll, that is still a pricey fast food lunch for Philly.  Still, it's a quality product and much better and cheaper than nearby options.  It also doesn't hurt that being steps away from the park gives diners the opportunity to enjoy their Luke's Lobster in the Rittenhouse sunshine.
llama_8b_pred_reasoning: The models show strong agreement, with BERT, LR, and SVM all predicting 4 stars, and the text sentiment being overwhelmingly positive, highlighting the quality of the lobster roll and the unique New England feel of the restaurant. So the word on the street was I needed to go check out the Oxford Exchange in downtown Tampa of which I've heard nothing but rave reviews. So Ryan and I booked a table for two Saturday, September 20 for brunch. 

Knowing the area and knowing exactly where it was located it was an easy find...It's right off of Kennedy as you make the bend heading towards downtown on the right-hand side. We parked right up front and entered and I have to say I was immediately impressed with the decor and feeling of the building. 

When you enter you feel like you're entering a 1920s establishment as Edison bulbs light the halls, dark rich mahogany walls and staircase adorned with an assortment of pictures the coffee and tea bar and the list goes on!! OMG entering for the first time was truly an experience in itself.... But I digress...

Being rather savvy people we were able to navigate our way to the hostess stand without any direction but I could see how some could be confused. 

We were set and immediately welcomed by our server who was very engaging and knowledgeable. I asked for a coffee Ryan a Mimosa both were delivered promptly and tasted delicious! As a sidenote they pride themselves on using Buddy Brew coffee which is located a few blocks up the road. The coffee was a very rich blend and definitely did the job..

After looking through the brunch menu which offered a good selection including breakfast items, lunch items as well as salads and soups. I ordered the bagel and salmon Ryan ordered the Crabcake Benedict (fancy) 

Both meals made it a timely fashion I would say under 10 minutes. Mine tasted wonderful the salmon was fresh and plentiful as well as the pickled onions and chive cream cheese over an everything bagel.

Ryan's tasted great the crab cakes tasted like crab and contained lumps of crab the hollandaise sauce was fantastic the potatoes on the other hand that came as a side dish were overdone and perhaps had been cooked prior. Other than that both meals were great as far as taste seasoning and presentation. 

Overall the experience was enjoyed and we  would deftly patronize this establishment again... 

Small nuances that would definitely add to the experience especially with the environment I feel the owners are trying to create would be as follows

I believe it was the floor manager a gentleman blonde hair black suit including a vest blue shirt and a tie standing in the dining room texting on his cell phone. 

And through my whole experience of around one hour I never saw anyone recognized as a manager doing table visits and checking on the guest experience... 
Other than that it was a wonderful experience and I would definitely recommend it to anybody wanting to experience something new and exciting as far as dining in downtown Tampa goes!!! 

Cheers!!
